Moreover, academia may be, but reality is not specialized. You're in Research? Breakthroughs don't come from keeping your head down and doing what you're told. That's a very corporate way of looking at the world. Real breakthroughs come from making connections nobody else has made before. If you see the world more as it really is, an undifferentiated, unspecialized mass of paradox and complexity, you'll do better science.

Your brain's loss of focus after 9 hours is a result of physically needing the neurological processes of sleep, especially neural pruning. Your co-workers are literally wearing ruts in their brains and soon literally won't have anything else but the ruts--no love, no joy, no hobbies, no enrichment--just work. They don't have any need for neural pruning because their lives are so monotone that there's no improvisation, no experimentation, just an endless droning of more cowbell.

Breakthroughs don't happen every day, though, so how do you keep your job in the meantime? Well, because you're living in the real world and thinking 360 degrees around them, you should be better than they are at two key skills: criticism and politics.

Criticism is easy. Science has a fucking massive reproducibility crisis. You can probably shoot holes in half of whatever your lab is churning out.

Of course, if you're the guy that kills each project, and this fucks up the grant money, then that won't work, which means you have to be better at politics. Scientists are humans just like the rest of us, despite their protestations to the contrary, which means they are petty and venal just like the rest of us.
